result.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
result.summary: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Compared with Agent S3, Chronotope reduces median end-to-end latency by 85.5% for a 27B model, expanding its performance envelope to 100% Live success at an 8-second deadline versus 0%. Chronotope enables real-time GUI control through compact interaction history, knowing when to preserve, revise, or replace actions, and an overall efficient architectural design that obviates verbose reflection, reasoning, and grounding calls.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 GUI agent 在思考期间界面变化导致的失败，提出环境变化、观察可用、决策提交与动作到达四个事件的 EODA 模型，并构建 ChronotopeGym（Paused/Replay/Live）诊断，同时给出保留紧凑交互历史、对挂起动作选择保留／更新／重决的 Chronotope 控制器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「动作在不同交互阶段失效」的失败分析与「何时保留、修订或替换待执行动作」的策略，与 LVR 中视觉证据时效、LOOK/STOP 调度和决策提交成本直接相关，可供核查四时钟分解能否迁移到 latent 推理的取证据与停止判断；论文本身不涉及内部 latent 表征。
